Name: Ashley Gregoire
Badge: Teacher as Researcher: Cultivating Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

After taking this course, I have much appreciation about "Say, Mean, and Matter" technique. I think it is important to look through primary sources and be able to investigate what they are saying and why they are saying it. Quotes and documents are not always cut and dry. They often need to be chunked and evaluated. My 8th grades have recently learned about Christopher Columbus and his actions towards the Taino populations. Christopher Columbus was the inventor of genocide and slavery towards the Taino people. He captured and tortured these poor people. I wanted to students to read about Christopher Columbus actions towards this people and make their own conclusions about his actions towards the Taino people.

Share one artifact or anecdote from trying out your chosen strategy (e.g., a piece of student work, notes from your Writer’s Notebook, a classroom snapshot, or a brief story from the experience).:
What new questions or next steps are you leaving this module with? How might you continue to explore or build on this inquiry in your future teaching?:

I have gained a better understanding on how to incorporate the "Say, Mean, and Matter" technique in my classroom. I think this will help my students understand the meaning behind each lesson.
